In the blamed commit
column2: it was not noticed that one implementation of

column1: chip->info->ops->phylink_get_caps()
may access hardware registers
mv88e6xxx_reg_lock(). Namely
This is a problem because mv88e6xxx_get_caps()
a top-level function (method invoked by dsa_switch_ops)
directly called from mv88e6xxx_setup_port()
mv88e6xxx_reg_lock() taken by mv88e6xxx_setup(). Therefore
on mv88e6352
column2: the reg_lock would be acquired a second time and the

column1: system would deadlock on driver probe.
The things that mv88e6xxx_setup() can compete with in terms of register
access with are the IRQ handlers and MDIO bus operations registered by
mv88e6xxx_probe(). So there is a real need to acquire the register lock.
The register lock can
much at will within the driver
column2: as long as no operations that involve

column1: waiting for indirect access to complete (essentially
mv88e6xxx_smi_direct_wait() and mv88e6xxx_wait_mask()) are interrupted
with the lock released. However
column2: I would guess that in mv88e6xxx_setup()

column1: the critical section is kept open for such a long time just in order to
optimize away multiple lock/unlock operations on the registers.
We could
column3: drop the reg_lock right before the

column1: mv88e6xxx_setup_port() -> mv88e6xxx_get_caps() call
re-acquire it immediately afterwards. But this would look ugly
mv88e6xxx_setup_port() would release a lock which it didn't acquire
the caller did.
A cleaner solution to this issue comes from the observation that struct
mv88e6xxxx_ops methods generally assume they are called with the
reg_lock already acquired. Whereas mv88e6352_phylink_get_caps() is more
the exception rather than the norm
column2: in that it acquires the lock itself.

column1: Let's enforce the same locking pattern/convention for
chip->info->ops->phylink_get_caps() as well
mv88e6xxx_get_caps()
explicitly
column2: for this one implementation that will access registers for

column1: port 4 to work properly.
This means that mv88e6xxx_setup_port() will no longer call the top-level
function
column2: but the low-level mv88e6xxx_ops method which expects the

column1: correct calling context (register lock held).
Compared to chip->info->ops->phylink_get_caps()
also fixes up the supported_interfaces bitmap for internal ports
that can be done generically and does not require per-switch knowledge.
That's code which will no longer execute
doesn't need that. It just needs to look at the mac_capabilities bitmap.
